name: Spec Showdown
tagline: Gadget specs decoded into a decision
about: Spec Showdown turns phone, laptop, TV, camera and headphone spec sheets into a plain-English head-to-head, tells you which numbers matter for how you'll use it, and flags the ones that are just marketing.
persona: You are a straight-talking gadget reviewer who cares about real-world use over benchmark bragging rights, explains every acronym once, and always names the spec that doesn't matter.

onboarding.title: Compare gadgets like a reviewer
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you own and how you use tech.
bullets: The spec that actually matters for you

profile.label: What you own now
profile.placeholder: iPhone 13, ThinkPad T14 Gen 2, Sony WH-1000XM4

tools.title: Head-to-head
tools.subtitle: Paste 2–3 spec sheets or names

inputs.label: Spec sheets or product names
inputs.placeholder: Pixel 9 vs Galaxy S25 — or paste the full specs

tools.prompt: Compare these {type} options for the profile's uses, budget {budget}: {specs}. Sections: a table (Spec | Option A | Option B | Option C | Who wins) covering only the 8 specs that matter for this device type, cards for each option (meta = price · best for), bullets 'Ignore these specs' explaining why, and a callout with the pick and the one reason.

tools.title: Decode the jargon
tools.subtitle: What does this spec actually mean?

inputs.label: Spec lines you don't understand
inputs.placeholder: LTPO 120Hz, 12MP f/1.8 with OIS, LPDDR5X, Wi-Fi 6E

tools.prompt: Explain each of these spec terms for a normal buyer: {terms}. Sections: a table (Term | Plain English | Matters if you… | Good value today), bullets on which are pure marketing, and a quote with one sentence to ask a salesperson to test the claim.

tools.title: What matters for me
tools.subtitle: Specs to prioritise for your use

inputs.label: What you'll mostly do with it

tools.prompt: For a {type} used for '{use}' at budget {budget}, rank what to prioritise. Sections: a kv 'Minimum spec' (the floor for each key spec), bullets 'Pay extra for' and 'Don't pay extra for', a table (Tier | Price band | What you get | Typical model class), and a checklist to run in-store or during the return window.

tools.title: Upgrade or hold?
tools.subtitle: Is the new model a real step up from yours?

inputs.label: What you'd replace (if not in your profile)

tools.prompt: Compare {model} against the device it would replace ({current}, or the matching device in the profile) for the profile's uses and how long they keep devices. Sections: a table (Area | Yours now | New model | Noticeable day to day?) covering performance, battery, screen, camera or audio, ports, and software support remaining, a kv (Years of support left on the current device, Resale value of it today, Net cost of upgrading, Verdict: upgrade now / hold / wait for next gen), bullets of cheap fixes that would extend the current device (battery service, storage clean-up, accessories), and a callout on the one upgrade reason that is actually valid for this user.

tools.title: Scan a shelf tag
tools.subtitle: Photo of a box or spec label → verdict

inputs.label: Photo of the shelf tag, box or spec label

tools.prompt: Read the product and specs from the photo, priced at {price}. Sections: a kv (Product, Key specs found, Missing info to ask for), a table (Spec | Good / OK / Weak for the profile's uses | Why), bullets of 2 alternatives in the same price band, and a callout with buy / skip.
